newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar listless, trapped in tight ranges.
newsitem.headline: Dollar listless, trapped in tight ranges.

text.p: The dollar traded quietly in a tight band on Monday, with little to pull it firmer or weaker against any of the major currencies, traders said.
"Basically the market didn't want to do anything with Tokyo and London out," one analyst said.
Little change is expected in the European session, where London is closed for the May Day holiday. Tokyo was closed for Children's Day.
A Japanese bank dealer in Singapore said there were at least $250-300 million worth of buying orders between 126.50 and 127.00 yen, but selling interest above 127.00 yen was weighing on the dollar.
"From tomorrow, I think Japanese investors will come in to buy dollars. I think it should go to 128 or 129 yen in the next two weeks," he said.
He said the Bank of Japan (BOJ) was unlikely to intervene above 127 yen.

"It's not a good time now because the market is not so long dollars. The investors will come in to buy the dollar on dips if it comes down on any intervention," he said, adding that the BOJ was more likely to come in at around 129 to 130 yen.
